candidates.name: Museo de Ferrocarril de Madrid
candidates.price: M-Th F before 14:00, holidays: €6 adult, €4 concession, free child under 4; F after 14:00, Sa Su €2.50
candidates.hours: Oct-May: Mon-Thu 09:30-15:00, Fri and holidays 10:00-18:00, Sat Sun 10:00-20:00; Jun-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-15:00
candidates.content: Museum with four railway tracks, exhibiting a large number of steam, diesel and electric locomotives used in Spain in the 19th and 20th century. Also on display are several model railways. Exhibits are described in Spanish only.

candidates.name: Estación de Chamberí
candidates.price: Free, booking from website (Spanish) linked from English site.
candidates.content: Former metro station designed by architect Antonio Palacios (creator of the Palacio de Cibeles, Círculo de Bellas Artes and Hospital de Maudes). It was inaugurated in 1919, but closed in 1966, thereby becoming a "ghost station". S

candidates.name: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales
candidates.alt: MCNM / National Museum of Natural Sciences
candidates.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat Sun and holidays 10:00-20:00; Sat Sun in Aug 10:00-15:00
candidates.content: Contains a large collection of fossils and minerals, plus educational exhibits (some are described in English but many are in Spanish only). Has two parts open to visitors with separate entrances. The ticket is purchased at the ma

candidates.name: Museo Geominero
candidates.content: Part of the Spanish Institute of Geology and Mining, this museum is dedicated to Geology (with a focus on Mineralogy) and Paleontology, containing an impressive collection of fossils and minerals discovered on the territory of Spa

candidates.name: Palacio Real
candidates.price: Entry €11; guided tour additional €4; students and children €6; free (disabled/teachers/children under 5); free M-Th 16:00-18:00 (Oct-Mar) and 18:00-20:00 (Apr-Sep) for EU citizens, legal residents, and citizens of Latin American countries (valid ID/passport required)
candidates.hours: Oct-Mar daily 10:00-18:00, Apr-Sep daily 10:00-20:00; last admission 1 hr before closing; closed occasionally for official ceremonies
candidates.content: The Palacio Real is an enormous palace, one of the biggest in Europe, with scorching plains of concrete around it. Though it is the official residence of the King of Spain, the royal family does not actually reside here and it is

candidates.name: Catedral de la Almudena
candidates.content: This massive cathedral faces the Palacio Real. Finished near the end of 20th century in the Neo-Gothic style, it is where the Princes of Asturias Felipe (current King Felipe VI) and Letizia were married in 2004. Especially notewor

candidates.name: Museo de San Isidro
candidates.alt: Los Orígenes de Madrid / San Isidro Museum
candidates.hours: Mid-Sep - Jun: Tue-Sun and holidays 09:30-20:00; Jul - mid-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00, closed Jan 1 and 6, May 1 and Dec 24, 25 and 31.
candidates.content: This is a museum of two parts. One part is dedicated to Saint Isidore the Laborer, while the other part is dedicated to the paleontology and archaeology of the region of Madrid from prehistory to 1561 (when Philip II made Madrid t

candidates.name: Museo de Historia de Madrid
candidates.content: This museum is dedicated to the history of Madrid from 1561 to present. Much of the history is explained by referencing exhibited paintings depicting people or events from the time, so it is also an art museum. Several maps and mo

candidates.name: Museo de América
candidates.hours: Tue-Sat 09:30-15:00, Thu 09:30-19:00, Sun and holidays 10:30-18:00; closed Jan 1, May 1, Dec 24, 25, 31
candidates.content: An excellent museum that many tourists miss. Houses thousands of artifacts from the Americas. The exhibit displays objects from many native cultures from before European conquest to colonial times and beyond. Don't miss the Tesoro

candidates.name: Museo del Traje
candidates.price: €3 (adults), €1.50 (concessions), free (students/children/seniors); free on Sa after 14:30, all day Su, and national holidays
candidates.hours: Tue-Sat 09:30-19:00, Sun and holidays 10:00-15:00; closed 1 and 6 Jan, 1 and 15 May, 24-25 and 31 Dec
candidates.content: Offers a wide selection of historical and more temporary costumes (from the early 1200s to now) which shows the aspects of different cultures and Spain. The museum also organizes many activities and events. The building itself won

candidates.name: Templo de Debod
candidates.hours: Oct-Mar: Tue-Fri 10:00-14:00 16:00-18:00, Sat Sun and holidays 09:30-20:00; Apr-Sep: Tue-Fri 10:00-14:00 18:00-20:00, Sat Sun and holidays 09:30-20:00; last admission 15 min before closing
candidates.content: An Egyptian temple in one of Madrid′s most beautiful parks. Near the Royal Palace and Plaza de España, it was a present given by Egypt to Spain for its role in saving the temple of Abu Simbel from the floodwaters of Lake Nasser fo

candidates.name: Palacio Real de El Pardo
candidates.content: It was built as a hunting lodge for the Spanish royal family, and was commandeered by Francisco Franco to serve as his residence. Today it serves as the official guest house for foreign dignitaries visiting Madrid, and is also ope

candidates.name: Museo del Prado
candidates.price: €15 (adults), €7.50 (seniors 65+), free (children/students under 25); free admission within 2 hours of closure; additional obligatory fee for special exhibits
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 10:00-20:00, Sun 10:00-19:00; closed/shortened hrs on some holidays; extended hrs for special exhibits; last admission 30 min before closing
candidates.content: One of the finest art collections in the world and the best collection of classical art in Madrid. It includes many different collections: the Spanish (El Greco, Velázquez, and Goya), the Flemish and Dutch (Rubens, van Dyck, and B

candidates.name: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía
candidates.alt: Museo Reina Sofía / Reina Sofía National Museum and Art Center
candidates.content: Housed in a former public hospital with an adjacent modern wing, this museum contains Spain's largest collection of 20th century art. Created to house Pablo Picasso's renowned Guernica, allowed after the return of democracy to Spa

candidates.name: CaixaForum Madrid
candidates.price: €6, free (La Caixa account holders), free on 15 May, 18 May, 9 Nov
candidates.content: A private centre particularly well-known for the 'vertical garden' by Patrick Blanc installed on a wall in front of the museum, as well as the quite special architecture of the building itself. The vertical garden can be seen from

candidates.name: Museo Naval de Madrid
candidates.content: A beautiful museum with a large interesting collection about Spanish naval history, from the efforts of kingdoms of Aragon and Castilia, the many successes and few failures (what's known in English as the defeat of the Spanish Arm

candidates.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
candidates.price: €3 (adults), €1.50 (concessions), free (seniors/students/children under 18); free Sa after 14:00 and Su
candidates.content: Small but interesting museum with artefacts and models from the indigenous people of Asia (mainly the Philippines, former colony of Spain), Africa and America. The exhibits are described in Spanish; however, on each floor, there i

candidates.name: Parque del Retiro
candidates.content: The main park of Madrid, the perfect place to take a rest during a sunny day, or take part in the drum circles around the statue of Alphonso XII on summer evenings. There is a large boating lake where one can hire a rowing boat -

candidates.name: Museo Lázaro Galdiano
candidates.price: €6 (adults), €3 (seniors/students/disabled), free (children under 12); free admission Tu-Sa 15:30-16:30 and Su 14:00-15:00
candidates.hours: Tue-Sat 10:00-16:30, Sun 10:00-15:00; closed Jan 1, Easter Thu and Fri, May 2 and 3, Nov 1, Dec 6 and 25
candidates.content: This museum houses the stunning collection of Spanish entrepreneur José Lázaro Galdiano (1862-1947) and is considered to be one of the best private collections in Spain. Not only will you find works by Goya, Velázquez, El Greco an

candidates.name: Museo Arqueológico Nacional
candidates.price: €3 (adults), €1.50 (concessions); free on Sa after 14:30, Su mornings, and national holidays
candidates.content: Don't let the sound of it frighten you. This large, well-designed museum opened again in April 2014 after several years of renovation works. It houses an incredible collection of archaeological finds from across the peninsula. It

candidates.name: Fundación Juan March
candidates.content: A few blocks off high-end shopping street Calle Serrano, this private foundation houses free temporary exhibitions of (mostly 20th-century) art which are often worth checking out. 10-15 min walk from either Museo Lázaro Galdiano o

candidates.name: Hospital de Maudes
candidates.content: Former hospital complex, built in 1916 in an eclecticist style (similar to Palacio de Cibeles, that was designed by the same architects). It includes a church, Santa María del Silencio. The hospital was intended to serve the poore

candidates.name: Museo Sorolla
candidates.price: €3 (adults), €1.50 (concessions); free admission Sa after 14:00 and all day Su
candidates.content: This museum is in what was the impressionist painter's house and features fine furniture and porcelain as well as his paintings.

candidates.name: Plaza Mayor
candidates.content: Perhaps the best known plaza in Madrid, this impressive square is now one of the main stops on any tourist visit. This enclosed square was built outside the city walls, and has played host to bullfights, markets, symphonies, tourn

candidates.name: Mercado de la Cebada
candidates.content: Once a glass and iron market of the late 19th century, it is now a vaulted concrete building which still serves as a neighborhood market. Where it used to stand an annexed public swimming pool and sports facilities, it lies now an

candidates.name: Real Ermita de San Antonio de la Florida
candidates.alt: Royal Chapel of St. Anthony of La Florida
candidates.hours: Closed in 2025 for conservation until further notice
candidates.content: This small church is famous for its murals, painted by Goya. It's also the mausoleum of the painter.

candidates.name: Parque de El Capricho
candidates.hours: Oct-Mar: Sat Sun and holidays 09:00-18:30 (last admission at 18:00); Apr-Sep: Sat Sun and holidays 09:00-21:00 (last admission at 20:30)
candidates.content: One of the most beautiful parks in Madrid. Built in 1797-1839, it has a strong Romanticism influence. Declared as an Historic Garden, its lakes with swans and ducks, labyrinths, palaces, squares and fountains makes this a lovely p

candidates.name: Plaza de Cibeles
candidates.content: A massive roundabout at the intersection of Calle de Alcala and Paseo del Prado, this plaza houses one of Madrid's emblems, the Fountain of Cibeles, which portrays the Roman goddess of fertility sitting upon a chariot pulled by tw

candidates.name: Banda Sinfónica Municipal de Madrid
candidates.content: Performs in El Retiro Park in the summer. Tickets can be purchased at the Teatro Monumental (listed above), at the tourist information centre in Plaza Mayor, and online.

candidates.name: Orquesta Nacional de España
candidates.content: Tickets are sold at ticket offices in the Auditorio Nacional de Música, Teatro María Guerrero, Teatro de la Zarzuela, Teatro de la Comedia, and Teatro Valle-Inclán.

candidates.name: Real Madrid
candidates.content: For football fanatics, a trip to the Santiago Bernabeu, the home of local club Real Madrid is not to be missed. Real Madrid is the most successful football club in Spain and Europe, having been crowned Spanish champions a record 3

candidates.name: Círculo de Bellas Artes
candidates.hours: Exhibits: Tue-Sun 11:00-14:00 17:00-21:00; Azotea: Mon-Fri 09:00-21:00, Sat Sun and holidays 11:00-21:00
candidates.content: A non-profit cultural center located a short walk from Sol, the CBA offers up a wide variety of events and shows including film, music, art displays, dance, theater and more. See the website (in Spanish) for a list of activities.

candidates.name: Cine Doré
candidates.content: This is a wonderful old Spanish theatre dating from the 1920s. It has three screens and shows mainly art-house and critically acclaimed films in the original language. In the summertime, they screen movies on the roof.

candidates.name: Matadero Madrid
candidates.hours: Usually Tue-Fri 16:00-21:00, Sat Sun 11:00-21:00, on Mon only the cinetheque is opened
candidates.content: Madrid's former main abattoir (matadero), an early 20th-century industrial brick compound in Arganzuela district, has been converted to an arts and cultural centre since the 2000s. It is intended to serve as a cross-disciplinary l

candidates.name: Auditorio Nacional de Música
candidates.hours: Ticket office: Mon 16:00-18:00, Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat 11:00-13:00; closed Sat in July and the month of Aug
candidates.content: The main concert venue for the Spanish National Orchestra and the Madrid Symphony Orchestra, as well as the main venue for touring classical artists and orchestras.

candidates.name: Atlético de Madrid
candidates.content: They play in La Liga, the top tier, and are one of the most successful teams in Spain, having won both La Liga and the Copa del Rey on ten occasions. They were European Cup runners-up in 2014 and 2016 and won the UEFA Europa Leagu

candidates.name: Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas
candidates.content: Arguably the most important bullfighting site in Spain. Unless you find this spectacle distasteful, this is a must see if you visit Madrid during the bullfighting season (May, during San Isidro). Tickets may nevertheless be expens

candidates.name: Yelmo Cineplex Ideal
candidates.content: Probably the best known V.O. (versión original, or original language) theatre in Madrid, it offers the largest selection of movies and is a short walk from Sol.

candidates.name: Rayo Vallecano
candidates.content: Rayo were relegated in 2019 so they now play in Segunda División, the second tier of Spanish football. Their home ground is Campo de Fútbol de Vallecas, capacity 15,000. It's in the Portazgo district, 2 km southeast of Atocha stat

candidates.name: Teatro Real
candidates.hours: Box office: Mon-Fri and Sat with performance 09:15-20:00, Sun and holidays 2 hrs before performance
candidates.content: The main opera theatre in Madrid. Tickets can be purchased online here.

candidates.name: Teatro de la Zarzuela
candidates.content: The Spanish version of the operetta (zarzuela) is performed here. This is also the main concert venue for the Community of Madrid Orchestra.

candidates.name: Orquesta de la Comunidad de Madrid
La Trashumancia
candidates.content: Annual event during which the centre of Madrid is free of cars and is instead filled with shepherds exercising their ancient right to drive sheep and livestock through the city.

candidates.name: Madrid Gay Pride
candidates.content: Annual event held between the last week of June and the first of July, with more than 1.5 million people in the street from all around the world. It began as a weekend party, but lately turned into a full-week extravaganza.

candidates.name: Corral de la Morería
candidates.content: One of the most famous flamenco tablaos in the world. It′s right in the heart of the city, and you can enjoy a full-fledged Spanish meal while you watch performances by renowned international flamenco music and dance artists.

candidates.name: Cuartel del Conde-Duque
candidates.hours: Box office: Tue-Sat 17:30-20:30; exhibits: Tue-Sat 10:00-14:00 17:30-21:00, Sun and holidays 10:30-14:00
candidates.content: This former military building now not only serves as a venue for musical, dance, and theatrical performances but also hosts contemporary art exhibits. Tickets for performances are also sold online.

candidates.name: Essential Flamenco
candidates.content: An authentic flamenco show in the heart of Madrid, set in a traditional exposed brick cave of the XIX century. Daily shows at 18:00, 19:30 and 21:00. Free drink included.

candidates.name: Libertad 8
candidates.content: Libertad 8 is an iconic coffee shop and bar located on Libertad del barrio de Chueca, in Madrid. Opened as a coffee shop in 1975, ever since then it's served as a stage for artists and singer-songwriters (known as cantautores). It

candidates.name: Museo Chicote
candidates.content: Voted the Best European Bar 2004 by MTV-Campari. Extensive cocktail list. Claims to have served drinks to many famous celebrities, including, Ava Gardner, Frank Sinatra, Lana Turner, Gary Cooper, Orson Wells, Yul Brynner and Ernes

candidates.name: Café de Oriente
candidates.content: Overlooks the Plaza Oriente and faces Palacio Real. Outdoor tables in summer, cozy indoor rooms in the cold months. Basement banquet room with a glass floor over ancient remains. Excellent food.

candidates.name: Café Comercial
candidates.content: Opened in the 1880s, this is the oldest cafe in Madrid, and has been run by the same family since the early 1900s. There's a modern internet café upstairs, but the downstairs remains traditional.

candidates.name: Areia
candidates.content: Very cool chill out bar decorated with deep colours in a Moroccan style. Dark and inviting. The seating includes cushions on the floor, traditional tables and chairs, or if you’re lucky, grab the four poster bed at the back.

candidates.name: El Junco Jazz Club
candidates.content: Smallish venue, starts the night with live jazz, later on morphs into relaxed night club. Not cheap (once inside, beer still €5.50, mixed drink €8.50), so attracts older crowd than others nearby.

candidates.name: Kapital
candidates.content: Enormous club with 7 floors. However, despite its popularity this club is usually not worth visiting. The owner has a policy to try to limit the number of foreigners in the club so if you are from anywhere except Spain, you will l

candidates.name: La Mallorquina
candidates.content: Famous for its pastries. Peaceful upstairs room where you can linger undisturbed over your café con leche and napolitana de chocolate (chocolate croissant).

candidates.name: Calle Cava Baja
candidates.content: This narrow street in La Latina is by far the most famous and popular place for tapas.

candidates.name: La Esquina de Eusebio
candidates.content: Trays of tapas are passed from one person to another in this typical bar of Madrid, absolutely not touristy but really worth it. And it's not so far from the centre.

candidates.name: The Sherry Corner
candidates.content: Sherry-tasting available in 8 languages. Commentary by knowledgeable oenologists explaining the details of the history, elaboration methods and tasting notes for each of the wines, while inviting guests to combine them with tapas

candidates.name: La Corolla
candidates.content: Specializes in delicious ‘tostas’ (small pieces of toast with different toppings) and avocado (aguacate), along with cañas (small beers).

candidates.name: Joy
candidates.content: Well known across Europe. Attracts at multi-national crowd. Popular with tourists as well as locals. It plays a mix of popular dance music. Every Thursday there is a Students Party.

candidates.name: El Tigre
candidates.content: Probably the most well-known tapas bar in Madrid, a must do. Don't get frightened by how crowded the bar is and go in anyway. This is one of the most lively places in the city! Get beers, big glasses of wine or un mini de mojito a

candidates.name: La Bola Taberna
candidates.content: A family-run restaurant operating since 1870 and serving traditional Madrileño cuisine. Reservations can be made online.

candidates.name: Freiduría de Gallinejas Embajadores
candidates.content: Another classic tapas bar in Madrid, not for conservative stomachs. Their most popular tapas are two of the most typical and traditional dishes in Madrid: gallinejas and entresijos. A treat for adventurous palates and lamb-lovers.

candidates.name: Chocolatería San Ginés
candidates.content: Specializing in chocolate con churros, this Madrid fixture is the perfect place to top off a night on the town. Also offers the usual assortment of coffees and teas.

candidates.name: Casa Lucio
candidates.content: Pricey but worth it. The Spanish Royal family sometimes entertain guests here and you may run into a few sports figures and movie stars. You should definitely book ahead on the weekends, and reservations are recommended even for t

candidates.name: Restaurante Botín
candidates.content: Opened in 1725, Botín is listed in the Guinness Book of Records as the oldest operating restaurant in the world. Once a favourite of Ernest Hemingway, the menu still delights with specialities including cochinillo (roast suckling

candidates.name: Tapería de Malasaña
candidates.content: Taperia with lunch room out the back. Reviews mixed about the tapas but great place for lunch; they do a great Cocido Madrileño and the house wine is more than acceptable (although served somewhat cold).

candidates.name: Restaurante Bar Rodrigo
candidates.content: Located behind the Mercado de Maravillas, this hidden gem in Tetuán serves affordable yet high-quality paellas that can compete with some of the best Madrid has to offer. Mostly patronized by locals, reservations are recommended,

candidates.name: Restaurante Malaysia
candidates.content: Authentic Malaysian food served right in the heart of San Blas, with an extensive menu drawing from the diverse culinary traditions of Malaysia and its neighbors.

candidates.name: Restaurante Samm
candidates.content: A Chamartín institution lauded as having some of the best paellas (if not the best) in Madrid, but only if you bring more than two people by order of the proprietor. Walk-ins turned away from Casa Benigna on the other end of Chama

candidates.name: Restaurante Casa Benigna
candidates.content: Owned by a Spanish-Norwegian family, this unassuming spot in Chamartín is known for serving traditional Spanish cuisine with a Nordic twist. Their paellas, served on custom-made copper pans, are reportedly among the best (if not t

candidates.name: Mercado de San Ildefonso
candidates.content: Streetfood market on Fuencarral street, right in the middle of the Malasaña-Chueca area. 15 different stalls offer arepas (cornmeal griddlecake), brochetas (skewer), tacos, tapas, ham, meats, wine, beer etc. Between late-May and e

candidates.name: Antigua Huevería
candidates.content: The very best huevos rotos ('broken eggs') and croquetas. Cheap, beautiful and delicious! The chicken-adorned tiled front dates from the 19th century.

candidates.name: El Rastro
candidates.content: Madrid's largest flea market, featuring rows upon rows of private vendors selling a variety of homemade goods, and a plethora of live entertainment. Many - but by no means all - stores along the side streets also open Sunday morni

candidates.name: Mercado de San Miguel
candidates.content: Near Plaza Mayor is this indoor market, identifiable by its ornate iron posts. Built in 1913, it's full of a wide range of high quality food. Even if you're not buying anything, it's worth entering for the sights and smells of dri

candidates.name: Cuesta de Moyano
candidates.content: A quaint outdoor book market.

december.text: Official taxis are white, and have a red stripe and the flag of Madrid on the front door. The tariff is displayed on top of the car – a 1 during daytime and a 2 at night, which become 2 and 3 on public holidays such as Christmas Eve.

Freiduría de Gallinejas Embajadores: Another classic tapas bar in Madrid, not for conservative stomachs. Their most popular tapas are two of the most typical and traditional dishes in Madrid: gallinejas and entresijos. A treat for adventurous palates and lamb-lovers.
Cines Dreams: This cinema is located in a shopping mall known for its ice-skating rink. It is a great place where teenagers can hang out since the mall also has restaurants, bars, and shops.

Palacio de Hielo: Popular with locals, especially among the residents of surrounding Hortaleza, this mall contains Madrid's only year-round ice skating rink (hence the name), as well as a gym, a bowling alley, a minigolf course and a swimming pool, plus a cinema and several shops and restaurants.

The Puerta del Sol square is Madrid's centre of the centre and therefore the symbolic omphalos of the whole kingdom. Here is milestone zero of Spain's road network from which all distances are measured. At least once a year, the whole nation looks here, when national TV stations broadcast the New Year's celebrations on
